title: Upper Deck Floor — Replacement of Seat Track Sections by Sealed Items in the Wet Bays
abstract: Replacement of the open seat track sections under the upper deck galleys and lavatories by sealed items, on aircraft delivered before the sealed section became the build standard.

sections.planning_reason: Corrosion has been found along the upper deck seat tracks wherever the track passes under a galley or a lavatory, with pitting to 0.4 mm and filiform attack extending several track pitches either side of the wet area. Twenty-two aircraft have been affected. The attack does not reduce the load capability at the depths found, but it makes seat leg removal difficult and has required track sections to be cut out under engineering repair on four aircraft.
sections.description: The open seat track sections in the bays under the galleys and the lavatories are removed and replaced by sealed track section webs ARD386097-40 with an integral elastomeric seal along the fastener line. The lower web sub-assembly D5350129109541 is removed and is not reused. The track splices are moved 60 mm outboard of their previous position and are pinned with clevis pins LN666073-13. A moulded drain channel is bonded to the track flange to take fluid to the existing floor drain.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove the seats, the galley and the lavatory monuments from the affected upper deck bays. Lift the floor panels and protect the exposed structure. Remove the fasteners along the track section to be replaced and lift out the section together with the lower web sub-assembly D5350129109541. Do a detailed visual inspection of the floor beam upper flange under the removed track and report any corrosion beyond the blend limit. Blend and re-protect where the finding is inside the limit. Position the sealed section web ARD386097-40 and drill the revised splice pattern using the jig. Deburr, apply the surface treatment and install the section wet with sealant. Install the clevis pins LN666073-13 at each splice. Bond the drain channel to the track flange and prove the drain path with water. Install the floor panels, the monuments and the seats. Do the seat track installation check of AMM-T-53-50-12-400-001-A and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TITAN-88 aircraft up to and including MSN T00130, that is those delivered before the sealed track section became the build standard. Aircraft that already carry the sealed section in some bays may have this Service Bulletin accomplished on the remaining bays only.
sections.material_note: Kits are ordered per bay rather than per aircraft, since operators convert only the bays under their own monument layout. Kit lead time is twenty-six weeks. Removed track sections are scrapped locally after the inspection findings have been reported.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next cabin refresh, or within 72 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

issue.reason: Pre-accomplishment check of the attachment fitting standard added to the effectivity statement and the bulletin scheduled for withdrawal on aircraft that take the titanium fitting.

Before accomplishment, establish the attachment fitting standard of the bay from the aircraft configuration record. On a bay that carries the titanium fitting this bulletin must not be applied: its instructions would have the mechanic machine a lug seat that no longer belongs there, and the material list orders items that are not correct for that bay. This bulletin is scheduled for withdrawal as each aircraft takes the fitting standard, and it is withdrawn in full once the fleet conversion closes; an operator whose bays are already at the fitting standard should treat it as cancelled today.

Do not draw a kit against a bay before the fitting standard of that bay has been checked; the sealed section in this kit is machined for the aluminium lug seat and cannot be fitted over the titanium fitting.
